transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I can’t stop fixating on how bad I look in every picture, and it’s starting to really interfere with my work and social life. It has just gotten so overwhelming lately and I don't know what to do.
When you think about these concerns, are you primarily worried about having a serious underlying medical illness, or is your distress specifically centered on your physical appearance?

No, I'm not worried about a medical illness at all; my distress is entirely about my physical appearance. I'm just deeply self-conscious about how I look in photos, especially with my nose looking huge and crooked and my skin being so uneven. It's just those specific things that bother me, not any health concerns.

Do you find yourself performing repetitive behaviors, such as constantly checking mirrors, seeking reassurance from others, or attempting to 'fix' these perceived flaws, because of your distress over your appearance?

Yes, I do those things constantly. I spend so much time taking dozens of selfies to check my angles, redoing my makeup to hide my nose and skin, and changing outfits multiple times before work. I also find myself zooming in on photos and constantly asking my mom or roommate if I look weird.
Do you ever find yourself thinking that others might be secretly judging or mocking your appearance, or are you primarily focused on the flaws themselves regardless of what others think?

It's really a mix of both, but it's heavily driven by my own intense focus on my huge, crooked nose and uneven skin, which I spend hours zooming in on and picking apart. At the same time, I do worry about how I look to others, which is why I'm constantly asking my mom or roommate if I look weird and avoiding being in photos or presenting in front of people.
Do you ever feel completely certain that others are staring at you or talking about your appearance, even when they tell you that they don't notice anything unusual?
I'm not really sure if people are actually staring or talking about me. I just feel incredibly self-conscious all the time and constantly worry that they might notice my flaws.
